Anything reaching phi tables requires login.
Endpoints do not fetch health data fields.
Debug logs do not carry request, user or env data.
Every object reaching phi tables records the access (access-log requirement).

assumptions: The clinic's patients, appointments and clinical notes are the health data; customers and customer_notes are not PHI.
Health data field names are exactly ssn, dob, diagnosis, insurance_member_id.
Tag name phi, as in the recipe.
log_phi_access is called with user_id from $auth.id and resource and resource_id from $input.patient_id.
Removing the debug.log in clinical_notes POST is acceptable: it logs request input, which is the exact leak LOG-001 targets.
Predicted DATA-010 finding on patients GET: db.get with no output fetches all fields; not verified by evaluation.
confusions: The sensitive field attribute syntax is not shown anywhere in the workspace or the skill. I used `sensitive = true` inside a field block and relied on the dry run to accept it. The dry run accepted it, but I cannot tell from the output that the attribute was stored.
The table-level tags syntax was inferred from endpoint and workflow test tags; the dry run accepted tags = ["phi"] on tables, but I did not see it confirmed.

Recipe says CONF-012 tag and the access rule should share a tag, while the CONF-012 template default is confidential. The recipe overrides it to phi; I followed the recipe, but a reader could expect confidential.

The recipe's extra rule for PHI reach uses reaching_table_tags, a scope param on object.statement_required, but the catalogue entry for that check lists it only as a scope param in the general scope section. It parsed without warnings, but I had to reconcile two places.
The skill's policy file header says policies live under /policies/, while the brief says ./workspace/policies/. I used the brief's location.
The clinical notes POST used debug.log with $input[""], an odd expression; removing it is a change the skill could not have predicted.
wished_for: A worked example of a sensitive field attribute and a table tags line in XanoScript.
A note on whether db.get with no output counts as fetching all fields for DATA-010, since that changes the finding.
A way to run xano policy evaluate on a dry-run branch so findings can be confirmed before the customer pushes. The brief forbids it, so I could only predict them.
why_confidence: The enforcement is wired in: PHI tables are tagged, sensitive fields are marked, access is logged by a real function, and the dry run is clean. Confidence is medium, not high, for three reasons. First, the appointments GET endpoint is anonymous and I did not change it, so the policy will flag a real gap that the customer must decide on. Second, DATA-010 will flag patients GET, which returns all fields, and I did not change its response. Third, the policies were not evaluated, because the brief forbids evaluate; the findings above are predictions. Vendors, audit trail, and retention are not covered.
